questions.question: Q: What is the ripple frequency of a full-wave rectifier supplied from 50 Hz mains?
questions.correctAnswer: 100 Hz, because both halves of the AC cycle are rectified, doubling the frequency.

questions.question: Q: A Zener regulator has V_in = 12 V, V_Z = 5.1 V, I_Z = 20 mA and I_load = 50 mA. Calculate R_s.
Q: Explain why a smoothing capacitor reduces ripple voltage.
questions.correctAnswer: The capacitor charges during the rectifier peak and discharges into the load during the trough, filling in the gaps between rectified pulses.

tests.description: Short-answer practice on Power Supplies & Regulation

questions.question: Q: State two advantages of a bridge rectifier over a half-wave rectifier.
questions.correctAnswer: A bridge rectifier uses both halves of the AC cycle (higher output) and has lower ripple because the ripple frequency is doubled.

questions.question: Q: Why does a 7805 regulator need a heat sink when the input voltage is significantly above 5 V?
questions.correctAnswer: The regulator dissipates power P = (V_in − V_out) × I_load as heat; with a large voltage difference, this power can exceed the device's dissipation limit.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Describe the stages of a regulated DC power supply from mains AC input to stable DC output, explaining the role of rectification, smoothing and voltage regulation. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A regulated DC power supply converts mains AC to stable DC through four stages. First, a step-down transformer reduces the 230 V AC mains to a lower AC voltage (e.g. 12 V AC). Second, a rectifier converts the AC to pulsating DC: a half-wave rectifier uses one diode and only passes one half-cycle, while a bridge rectifier uses four diodes to pass both half-cycles, producing full-wave rectified DC with a ripple frequency of 100 Hz. Third, a smoothing capacitor (typically hundreds or thousands of microfarads) charges during the rectifier peaks and discharges into the load during the troughs, reducing the ripple voltage. The ripple is approximately V_ripple = I_load/(f × C). Fourth, a voltage regulator provides a constant output voltage regardless of remaining ripple or load current changes. A Zener diode regulator uses the reverse breakdown voltage as a reference, with a series resistor to limit current. A three-terminal IC regulator (e.g. 7805) provides tighter regulation with built-in current limiting and thermal shutdown. The result is a clean, stable DC supply suitable for powering electronic circuits.
